about.title: McFarland Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: A wrongful death claim in McFarland is not about reopening a wound. It gives the people left behind a way to hold someone accountable and steady a household that has lost its footing. McFarland is a small Kern County town of about 14,658 people, and public records list one traffic death here in 2025. One is a number that fits neatly on a page, but in a place this size it is a neighbor, a coworker, a parent in the school pickup line. Local collision reports cluster along SR-99, Elmo Highway, Driver Road and Garzoli Avenue, routes many residents drive daily toward Delano, Bakersfield and the surrounding farmland. Under California law, a spouse, domestic partner or child can bring a civil wrongful death action, separate from any criminal case, and the deadline generally runs two years from the date of death. LawProactive is a free service. We listen to what happened, then connect you with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency, so nothing is owed unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why McFarland Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: We sort out who has the right to file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to the spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney we connect you with can confirm where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: We respect the two-year clock
items.desc: A wrongful death action generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. Reaching out early keeps your options intact.

items.title: We understand what losses count
items.desc: Recoverable losses include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship and guidance. Every attorney in our network works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on SR-99 near McFarland. Does the highway location change the claim?
items.answer: It can. SR-99 is a state highway, and if a road condition or public agency contributed to the death, part of the claim may be against a government entity. Those claims carry a much shorter deadline than the usual two years, often measured in months rather than years. An attorney can evaluate quickly whether that path applies to your situation.

items.question: There is a criminal case against the driver. Do we have to wait for it to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action that runs on its own track, separate from any criminal prosecution in Kern County. The two cases can proceed at the same time, and the outcome of one does not decide the other. Waiting for the criminal case to end can also eat into your civil filing deadline.

items.question: I am the deceased's sibling. Can I bring a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Standing goes first to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and the children. Siblings and other relatives generally qualify only in certain circumstances, such as when there is no spouse or child, or when they were financially dependent on the person who died. The attorney LawProactive connects you with can review your family's specific situation and explain who is eligible.
